source_evidence: A 401(k) plan is an employer-sponsored retirement plan that gives employees a choice of investment options, often various mutual funds.
answer: A 401(k) plan lets employees choose among investment options offered through the plan, often including mutual funds. A target date fund is one popular type of fund in 401(k) plans. Some options held within retirement accounts may be structured as collective investment trusts (CITs), which the source notes are not regulated by the SEC. These are different kinds of investment options—not the traditional and Roth account options, which describe how contributions and taxes are handled.
